title: Use a Graphical User Interface (GUI)-based word processor to create and edit documents

lessons.title: Opening the word processor and typing a document
lessons.html:
What is a word processor?

A word processor is a computer program for writing letters, lists and reports. Examples are Microsoft Word, LibreOffice Writer and Google Docs. GUI means you use a mouse or touchpad to click on pictures (icons) and menus on the screen.

On a farm you can use it to write a list of workers for a shift, a notice about a meeting, a feed order, or a letter to the co-op.

Parts of the screen

  • Title bar: at the top. It shows the name of your document.
  • Menu or ribbon: words and icons like File, Home, Insert. You click them to do things.
  • Work area: the big white page where you type.
  • Cursor: the small flashing line. It shows where the next letter will go.
  • Scroll bar: on the side. Use it to move up and down the page.

Start a new document

  1. Click the word processor icon to open it.
  2. Click File, then New, then Blank document.
  3. Start typing.

Useful keys

KeyWhat it does
EnterStarts a new line or paragraph
BackspaceDeletes the letter to the left of the cursor
DeleteDeletes the letter to the right of the cursor
ShiftHold it to type a capital letter
Space barPuts a space between words
Arrow keysMove the cursor

Do not press Enter at the end of every line. The program moves to the next line by itself. Press Enter only when you want a new paragraph.

Sit straight, keep the screen at eye level and rest your eyes every so often.

lessons.title: Saving, editing and formatting
lessons.html:
Save your work

If you do not save, your work can be lost when the power goes off. Save early and save often.

  1. Click File, then Save As.
  2. Choose a folder, for example Documents.
  3. Type a clear name, for example Feed order March.
  4. Click Save.

After the first time, you can click Save or press Ctrl and S together.

Select text

To change words, you first select them. Put the cursor before the word, hold the left mouse button and drag over the words. They turn a different colour. Now you can change them.

Edit text

  • Delete: select the words and press Delete.
  • Copy: select, then press Ctrl and C. Click where you want it and press Ctrl and V to paste.
  • Move (cut): select, press Ctrl and X, click the new place and press Ctrl and V.
  • Undo: made a mistake? Press Ctrl and Z.

Format text

Formatting changes how the words look.

  • Bold: makes words dark and strong. Good for headings.
  • Italic: makes words lean.
  • Font size: makes letters bigger or smaller.
  • Alignment: left, centre or right. Centre is good for a heading.
  • Bullets: make a list with dots.

Check spelling

A red wavy line under a word means it may be spelt wrong. Right-click the word to see suggestions. Always read your document yourself too.

Print

Click File, then Print. Check the printer name and number of copies, then click Print.

Key points

  • Open a new document with File, New.
  • Save often with a clear file name.
  • Select text before you change it.
  • Use Ctrl and Z to undo a mistake.
  • Check spelling, then print.
